name: Lateral Squat Walk
summary: A lower-body exercise performed in a partial squat while stepping sideways to strengthen the hip abductors and glutes.

setup: Stand tall with your feet parallel and hip-width apart.
Hinge slightly at the hips and bend your knees to lower into a quarter or half squat.
Keep your chest upright, spine neutral, and hands held together in front of your chest for balance.
steps: Step laterally to the side with your lead foot, widening your stance while maintaining the squat depth.
Slowly bring the trailing foot inward until feet return to hip-width apart.
Continue stepping in the same direction for the target number of reps or distance, then repeat in the opposite direction.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and rhythmically throughout the set without holding your breath.
cues: Stay low throughout the entire set
Push through the hips, not the lower back

common_faults.correction: Maintain a constant squat depth without bobbing up and down.

common_faults.fault: Turning toes outward excessively during lateral steps.
common_faults.correction: Keep your toes pointed forward so the lateral glutes remain under active tension.

common_faults.fault: Letting the feet touch together on the follow-through step.
common_faults.correction: Stop the trailing foot when it returns to hip-width apart to maintain continuous hip tension.

precautions: Ensure the floor path is completely clear of tripping hazards before stepping sideways.
